newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business News - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business News - July 29.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BA APPEALS TO BLAIR IN EURO ROW OVER SLOTS

British Airways is looking for government support in its battle with the European Commission for concessions so it can proceed with its alliance with American Airlines. Competition commissioner Karel van Miert has demanded BA surrender 350 take off and landing slots per week at Heathrow, so that the merged company will not be capable of dominating business - a figure which is over twice the amount initially set out by the director general of Fair Trading. It is believed the two sides may comprom ise at between 200 and 250 slots per week.
-- SETBACK FOR NEWS CORP DEAL

News Corporation and Heritage Media have stated their merger could be put into question, as the US Department of Justice has launched an investigation into the deal concerning its possible effect on competition. News Corp, which previously agreed to sell Heritage's radio and television businesses to comply with anti-trust rules, has agreed to extend the period of time allotted to the anti- trust division to challenge or allow the deal to close.
-- BOOKER IN SLIMLINE SUCCESS

The Booker food group has disclosed it is ahead of schedule in its integration of the Nurdin & Peacock cash-and-carry group it acquired in 1996 for 267m stg. Booker has closed the head Nurdin office in south London, which employed 380 staff, only 30 of which were transferred to Booker's headquarters in Northamptonshire. Booker's future plans involve streamlining its operations through the closure of at least 25 depots and the loss of about 1,200 jobs.
THE TIMES
-- CONCERN RAISED ON UTILITY REGULATION

The Electricity Consumers' Committee watchdog has requested the government suspend its plans for utility regulation until after 2000, due to fears it would create an environment of uncertainty when combined with the entry of competition to the gas and electricity sectors. The request echoes a similar warning from Ofgas' Clare Spottiswoode, who stated plans to put the interest of the consumer and environmental factors at the heart of regulation were unworkable.
-- NBTY IN TALKS FOR HOLLAND & BARRETT

US vitamin manufacturer NBTY is in talks with health food chain Holland & Barrett concerning its possible acquisition of the chain, put up for sale by German group Gehe at 130m stg. NBTY chairman Scott Rudolph declared the acquisition of the over-400 store chain to NBTY's existing 100 US locations would come as part of its 'strategic plan' to expand its retail division.
-- ONE 2 ONE INTRODUCES PRE-PAYMENT

Mobile phone operator One-2-One has initiated the first pre-payment scheme to be offered on digital service, in an attempt to deal with the growing number of customers in debt and to attract new customers who flinch at the thought of long contracts and monthly charges. The system will be known as Up 2 You, and will be sold to customers as a handset and access package, with vouchers available from a variety of locations including Sainsbury's and post offices.
THE GUARDIAN
-- DOLE DISCIPLINE TO BACKFIRE ON DEMORALISED

A report from the Employment Policy Institute has warned the government its welfare-to-work scheme may meet with failure, as it seeks to 'discipline' those already disheartened by long periods of time on benefits. Alan Deacon, a professor of social policy at the University of Leeds, commented threats against those already doing all they could to find a job were useless and the EPI added the government needed to ensure its four employment incentive options were good enough to attract youngsters.
-- BENETTON RUMOURS FAIL TO SILENCE PUMA ROAR

Rumours that Benetton was seeking to acquire the Puma sportswear group led shares in the latter to rise dramatically on the Frankfurt stockmarket, despite denials by both groups of any takeover. Puma released disappointing half-year results on Friday, stating full year sales growth will be in single figures due to difficulty in the US market, and resulted in a downgrade from Goldman Sachs and Commerzbank.
-- ENERGIS ON COURSE

The telecommunications arm of National Grid, Energis, has revealed it is in talks with mobile phone operator Vodafone. The two groups are discussing a joint marketing deal to offer customers advanced fixed and integrated phone services, which Energis would use to help it break into the residential and small business markets.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SIMS LOSES 31M STG ON SALE OF RETAIL BUSINESS

Troubled meat processor Sims Food has sold its retail business to Dawn Holdings, a private Irish group, for 12.1m stg. The sale amounted to a loss of 31.1m stg for Sims, as the retail arm had an annual turnover of 112m stg and made an operating profit of 2.9m stg in the year to March. The deal is expected to reduce borrowings at the group from 16m stg to about 5.5m stg.
-- ORIENTAL RESTAURANT SIGNS UP KEN HOM

Oriental Restaurant Group, the AIM-listed Far Eastern restaurant chain, has hired television presenter Ken Hom to lead the group into the continental European market through establishing a chain of restaurants. Oriental will use Hom's name and specially designed dishes in their restaurants in return for an undisclosed consultancy fee and share options dependent on the success of the new chain.
-- FUTURE INTEGRATED SHARES PLUNGE ON PROFIT WARNING

Telecom and computer systems group Future Integrated Technology has shocked investors with the announcement it expects a 600,000 stg loss when it reports its results for the year to May 1997. Future labelled the losses 'growing pains', caused by a period of rapid expansion of activities and personnel, combined with a relocation of premises and emphasis on larger, corporate contracts. The warning led share prices to tumble from 140p to 85.5p.
